title: WL-MT403-WindowsBrokerAndPortableWpLifecycle
clause: Implement the lazy one-store-per-project-and-WP lifecycle behind a single Handshake-owned Windows broker and a disk-agnostic locator.

conditional_execution.approved: Execute this contract normally after MT-402.
conditional_execution.rejected: Do not edit product code or create local state; record validator-checked NOT_APPLICABLE_BY_MT401_REJECTION.

scope.summary: GOAL: If and only if MT-401 authorizes evaluation, implement one Handshake-owned broker that is the sole Windows process allowed to open WP-local database files. A store is created lazily for exactly one WpLocalStoreKey(project_id, wp_id) when canonical SurrealDB records an approved working-store need. Every session, MT and worktree in the WP routes through the same broker instance and logical database. The portable locator is relative to an operator-configured Handshake managed-state root and never treats a worktree, session folder or absolute machine path as authority.
forbidden_paths: Any database under a git worktree or session/MT directory
Any Turso Cloud URL, token, push, pull, sync or remote connection
Any second process opening a WP-local database file
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning requires an approved MT-401 exception, a canonical existing project and WP read from SurrealDB, an explicit local-store-needed decision, and an authenticated broker request; otherwise it returns a typed error and creates nothing.

Exactly one logical database is addressed by each (project_id, wp_id). Ten sessions, repeated MT IDs and multiple worktrees for the same WP resolve the same broker/store identity, while the same wp_id in another project resolves a different identity.

On Windows, only the Handshake broker process opens the file. Other Handshake components use typed IPC/in-process broker calls, and direct open attempts from a second process or stale broker generation fail with WP_LOCAL_STORE_BROKER_OWNERSHIP_DENIED.

The locator stores a normalized relative identifier under an operator-configured managed-state root. SurrealDB stores only the portable locator and broker metadata, never a drive letter, user-profile path, credential or raw encryption key.
Moving the managed project and its configured state root to another disk preserves project_id/wp_id identity and re-resolves the store without editing canonical records or searching arbitrary disks.
No DB is created per project, subproject, task, prototype, session, MT or worktree merely because it exists; provisioning is per WP and lazy only.
Broker startup, open, close and failure are quiet background operations that do not create a foreground window, steal focus or accept keyboard input.
proof_targets: Run a Windows integration test with two worktrees and concurrent sessions for one WP and independently inspect open handles to prove one broker-owned database file.
Run negative direct-open, stale-generation, wrong-project and unrequested-WP tests and verify zero filesystem side effects.
Move a disposable managed-state root between two absolute locations, restart Handshake and prove the same portable locator resolves the same project/WP state.
Scan source and runtime configuration for cloud sync, URL/token and direct engine-open paths outside adapter_turso.rs.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Broker and lifecycle backend only. MT-409 provides the operator surface; trace state must expose broker generation and lifecycle state without absolute paths.

target_entries: WP-local working store > One database per Work Packet
WP-local working store > Windows broker and portable location

same_project_private_resource_cases: A project member without the exact WP/source grant cannot open the broker handle or infer local state.
cross_account_negative_cases: Direct open, a second process and a forged project/WP locator cannot access another account's database.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Broker handles retain the source AccessSpace and cannot be transferred to a broader session.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or project/AccessSpace switch invalidates active handles and requires a fresh canonical membership read.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: No remote Turso, SaaS, MCP, replica or synchronization endpoint is reachable through the broker.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Portable locators and diagnostics redact absolute roots, usernames, keys, content and unauthorized store existence.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Provision, broker generation and lifecycle transitions require bounded correlation receipts but cannot contain local payloads or keys.
Ownership, locator and lifecycle failures need stable reason codes and recovery actions.
The persistent broker is a declared Handshake-owned background process/service and must expose bounded health and process identity.

risk_if_missed: Multiple file openers or worktree-local databases can corrupt state, fork a WP across agents, break project moves and create hidden per-session authorities.

risks: A worktree helper opens the file directly for convenience.
Crash restart spawns a new broker while the prior generation still owns a handle.
Absolute paths leak into SurrealDB or move logic scans arbitrary disks.
Every nested project node receives a database despite having no WP need.
minimum_controls: Single broker ownership token/generation and second-open denial.
Windows handle, ACL, restart and project-move proofs.
